$comment: D-EVT-22, plan-1378 §5: the bridge events of 1378 to 1444 for South, East and Southeast Asia, Africa and the Americas. Same shape as events-campaign.json; they join only a campaign that starts before 1444 (EVT-095). An event whose id is already in events-campaign.json replaces it there (a 1444 event re-dated to its conditions, EVT-096). entities names realms the game does not know yet; places maps new place keys to map provinces. Sources: start-date/research/asia.md and africa-americas.md (section F of each part).

colla_lupaca_war.name: The Colla and the Lupaca at war

faruqi_grant_thalner.name: Thalner granted to Malik Raja Faruqi

ho_dynasty.name: Hồ Quý Ly takes the throne

majapahit_collapse.name: Collapse of Majapahit and rise of Demak

tepanec_war.name: The Tepanec war and the Triple Alliance

treasure_fleet_on_the_swahili_coast.name: Ming fleets on the Swahili coast

localization.event.air_sultanate_founded.desc: Tired of feuding among themselves, the Tuareg confederations of Aïr send for a sultan to judge between them. His seat is first near Takedda and moves to Agadez around 1430, on the caravan road from the Hausa cities north.
localization.event.air_sultanate_founded.name: The Aïr sultanate
localization.event.air_sultanate_founded.option.accep: Take a sultan who pays tribute to Mali
localization.event.air_sultanate_founded.option.choos: Choose a sultan to judge between the clans
localization.event.air_sultanate_founded.option.raid_: Stay free clans and raid Gobir
localization.event.arakan_restored_at_mrauk_u.desc: After more than twenty years of exile at Gaur, Min Saw Mon returned in 1429 with an army lent by the Sultan of Bengal. He retook Arakan and in 1430 founded a new capital at Mrauk U, paying tribute to Bengal and using Muslim titles beside his Buddhist ones.
localization.event.arakan_restored_at_mrauk_u.name: Arakan restored at Mrauk U
Keep peace with Ava and leave him in Gaur
Restore him as a free ally
Restore Min Saw Mon as Bengal's tributary
localization.event.ava_takes_arakan.desc: In 1406 Minkhaung of Ava sent his son Minye Kyawswa over the Arakan Yoma; King Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal and Ava's man was put on the throne at Launggyet. Pegu soon struck back and installed its own client, turning Arakan into a front of the Forty Years' War.
localization.event.ava_takes_arakan.name: Ava takes Arakan
localization.event.ava_takes_arakan.option.install_ar: Keep a client king at Launggyet
localization.event.ayutthaya_sacks_angkor.desc: After decades of Siamese raids, King Borommarachathirat II of Ayutthaya besieged Angkor around 1431 and took it, carrying off its Brahmins, regalia and statues. The Khmer court abandoned the old capital and moved south-east towards the Mekong at Phnom Penh.
localization.event.ayutthaya_sacks_angkor.name: Ayutthaya takes Angkor
localization.event.ayutthaya_sacks_angkor.option.inst: Make the Khmer king a tributary
localization.event.ayutthaya_sacks_angkor.option.sack: Take Angkor and carry off its court
localization.event.bahmani_takes_velama_forts.desc: Once the Velamas of Rachakonda went over to Vijayanagara, Ahmad Shah Bahmani took Warangal in 1424, and the Velama forts of Rachakonda and Devarakonda fell by c.1435. Ahmad Shah moved his capital to Bidar in 1429 to hold the east.
localization.event.bahmani_takes_velama_forts.name: The Bahmanis take Telangana
Take the Velama forts and annex Telangana
localization.event.battle_of_buir_lake.desc: Lan Yu crosses the Gobi and surprises the khan's camp at Buir Lake, capturing tens of thousands of people and the court's seals. Tögüs Temür flees west with a handful of riders; the Yuan restoration is over.
localization.event.battle_of_buir_lake.name: Battle of Buir Lake
localization.event.bengal_azam_shah_revolt.desc: Prince Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah rose against his father Sikandar Shah and killed him at Goalpara in 1390. Azam Shah went on to patronise Persian poets and open relations with the Ming.
localization.event.bengal_azam_shah_revolt.name: Azam Shah's revolt
localization.event.bengal_azam_shah_revolt.option.the: The prince takes the throne by the sword
localization.event.chanka_war.desc: The Chanka confederation crosses the Apurímac and marches on Cusco. Old Viracocha Inca withdraws, but his son Inca Yupanqui stays to fight, wins, and takes the name Pachacuti.
localization.event.chanka_war.name: The Chanka war
localization.event.chanka_war.option.flee_with_viraco: Flee with Viracocha and pay the Chanka
localization.event.chanka_war.option.stand_with_inca_: Stand with Inca Yupanqui and defend Cusco
localization.event.chimor_expansion.desc: Having secured Lambayeque, the kings of Chan Chan send their armies down the coast to Casma and Huarmey, building canals and setting governors over the valleys.
localization.event.chimor_expansion.name: Chimor reaches south
localization.event.chimor_expansion.option.conquer_th: Conquer the valleys to the south
localization.event.chimor_expansion.option.rule_throu: Rule them through their own lords
localization.event.colla_lupaca_war.desc: Colla Capac of Hatuncolla and Cari of Chucuito fight for the herds and fields of Lake Titicaca. Both sides look to Cusco for help.
localization.event.colla_lupaca_war.name: The Colla and the Lupaca at war
localization.event.colla_lupaca_war.option.back_the_l: Back the Lupaca and win a friend on the lake
localization.event.colla_lupaca_war.option.stay_out: Stay out of the lake wars
localization.event.courts_of_japan_reunited.desc: With Kyushu won by Imagawa Ryōshun and the Yamana broken, the Southern emperor Go-Kameyama returns to Kyoto and hands the regalia to Go-Komatsu, on the promise that the two lines will take turns on the throne.
localization.event.courts_of_japan_reunited.name: Courts of Japan reunited
localization.event.courts_of_japan_reunited.option.fi: Fight on in the Yoshino mountains
localization.event.courts_of_japan_reunited.option.me: Hand over the regalia on the promise of alternation
localization.event.cusco_basin_wars.desc: The kings of Cusco fight, raid and marry their way past the Ayarmaca and the small lordships of the valley until the whole basin answers to Cusco.
localization.event.cusco_basin_wars.name: Cusco masters its basin
localization.event.cusco_basin_wars.option.absorb_the: Absorb the Ayarmaca and the basin lords
localization.event.death_of_che_bong_nga.desc: In February 1390 Chế Bồng Nga, the Cham king who had sacked Thăng Long three times, was shot dead aboard his flagship at Hải Triều when a defector pointed out his ship to the Viet gunners. His general La Khai took the throne and pulled back, and Champa's great offensive was over.
localization.event.death_of_che_bong_nga.name: Death of Chế Bồng Nga
localization.event.death_of_che_bong_nga.option.cham_: Fight on for the Ô and Lý lands
localization.event.death_of_che_bong_nga.option.la_kh: La Khai takes the throne and falls back to Vijaya
localization.event.death_of_firuz_shah.desc: Firuz Shah Tughlaq died in September 1388, near eighty, after his heir Fath Khan and then his son Muhammad had failed him. The throne went to his grandson Tughlaq Shah II, and the nobles' wars began.
localization.event.death_of_firuz_shah.name: Death of Firuz Shah
localization.event.death_of_firuz_shah.option.prince_: Let Prince Muhammad hold the court
localization.event.death_of_hayam_wuruk.desc: Hayam Wuruk, the king under whom Majapahit claimed tribute from half the archipelago, died in 1389. His son-in-law Wikramawardhana took the throne at Trowulan, but his own son Bhre Wirabhumi kept an eastern court of his own, and the two lines drifted towards war.
localization.event.death_of_hayam_wuruk.name: Death of Hayam Wuruk
localization.event.death_of_hayam_wuruk.option.single: Unite the royal lines under one heir
localization.event.death_of_hayam_wuruk.option.two_co: Wikramawardhana reigns while Bhre Wirabhumi keeps the east
localization.event.death_of_hongwu.desc: Hongwu dies in 1398, aged seventy. His heir Zhu Biao died in 1392, so the throne passes to the grandson Zhu Yunwen, the Jianwen Emperor, over the heads of his uncles who command the frontier armies.
localization.event.death_of_hongwu.name: Death of the Hongwu Emperor
localization.event.death_of_hongwu.option.name_the_pr: Pass the throne to the Prince of Yan
localization.event.death_of_tezozomoc.desc: The old tlatoani of Azcapotzalco dies after a reign of half a century. His son Maxtla pushes aside the chosen heir, and the Mexica king Chimalpopoca is killed.
localization.event.death_of_tezozomoc.name: Death of Tezozómoc
localization.event.death_of_tezozomoc.option.tayatzin: Tayatzin succeeds as his father wished
localization.event.death_of_togus_temur.desc: Fleeing from Buir Lake, the khan Tögüs Temür is murdered on the Tula by Yesüder, an Arigh Böke descendant backed by the Oirat. The Kublaid line ends and the western Mongols become a power of their own.
localization.event.death_of_togus_temur.name: Death of Tögüs Temür
localization.event.death_of_togus_temur.option.a_kubl: A Kublaid heir holds the khanship
localization.event.death_of_togus_temur.option.yesude: Yesüder seizes the throne with Oirat swords
localization.event.ewuare_accession.desc: Ewuare seizes Benin's throne after a war of succession that burns much of the city. He rebuilds Benin City behind its walls, curbs the old uzama chiefs and starts the conquests that make Benin a forest empire.
localization.event.ewuare_accession.name: Ewuare the Great
localization.event.ewuare_accession.option.rebuild_an: Rebuild the city and curb the uzama
localization.event.ewuare_accession.option.rule_with_: Rule with the consent of the uzama chiefs
localization.event.fall_of_mayapan.desc: The Xiu and the lords living at Mayapan rise against the Cocom and their Canul mercenaries. The league's walled capital is sacked and abandoned, and Yucatán splits into rival provinces.
localization.event.fall_of_mayapan.name: Fall of Mayapan
localization.event.fall_of_mayapan.option.crush_the_r: Send the Canul mercenaries against the lords
localization.event.fall_of_mayapan.option.share_power: The Cocom share power with the Xiu
localization.event.fall_of_mayapan.option.the_xiu_des: Mayapan falls and the provinces go their own way
localization.event.fall_of_xaltocan.desc: The Tepanecs and their Cuauhtitlan allies end the long feud with Otomí Xaltocan. The town is taken and its people flee to Metztitlan and the Acolhua lands.
localization.event.fall_of_xaltocan.name: Fall of Xaltocan
localization.event.fall_of_xaltocan.option.make_it_tr: Leave Xaltocan its lords and take tribute
localization.event.fall_of_xaltocan.option.take_the_l: Take Xaltocan and scatter the Otomí
localization.event.faruqi_grant_thalner.desc: Firuz Shah granted Thalner on the Tapti to Malik Raja Faruqi, a captain of his guard, to hold the southern frontier against the Bahmanis. The Faruqis made the fief the kingdom of Khandesh.
localization.event.faruqi_grant_thalner.name: Thalner granted to Malik Raja Faruqi
localization.event.faruqi_grant_thalner.option.grant_: Grant Thalner to the Faruqi as a march
localization.event.faruqi_grant_thalner.option.keep_a: Keep the frontier under a salaried governor
localization.event.forty_years_war.desc: From 1385 Ava's kings marched down the Irrawaddy again and again to win the Mon ports, and Razadarit of Pegu threw them back each time. The war of Ava and Pegu ran with truces until 1424 and left both realms where they started.
localization.event.forty_years_war.name: The Forty Years' War
localization.event.forty_years_war.option.ava_marches: Ava marches on the Mon ports
localization.event.forty_years_war.option.truce_on_th: Agree a truce along the frontier
localization.event.gelug_founded.desc: Tsongkhapa holds the first Great Prayer Festival at Lhasa and founds Ganden monastery in 1409 with the gongma's patronage. Drepung and Sera follow, and his reformed Gelug school grows into Tibet's greatest.
localization.event.gelug_founded.name: Founding of the Gelug
localization.event.gelug_founded.option.favour_the_ol: Keep favour with the Karmapa and Sakya
localization.event.goryeo_raids_tsushima.desc: After decades of wokou raids on its coasts and grain ships, Goryeo sends Bak Wi with a hundred warships against Tsushima, burning pirate ships and freeing captives.
localization.event.goryeo_raids_tsushima.name: Goryeo strikes Tsushima
localization.event.goryeo_raids_tsushima.option.forti: Fortify the coasts and settle surrendered pirates
localization.event.great_law_of_peace.desc: The Peacemaker and Hiawatha persuade the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca to end their feuds. Their chiefs meet in one council under the Great Law.
localization.event.great_law_of_peace.name: The Great Law of Peace
localization.event.great_law_of_peace.option.feuds_go: Let each nation go its own way
localization.event.great_law_of_peace.option.found_th: Found the League of the Five Nations
localization.event.gujarat_independence.desc: Zafar Khan, Delhi's governor of Gujarat since 1391, was pressed by his son Tatar Khan to march on Delhi in 1403. After Tatar Khan's death Zafar Khan was proclaimed Sultan Muzaffar Shah, c.1407.
localization.event.gujarat_independence.name: Gujarat breaks away
localization.event.gujarat_independence.option.march_: Follow Tatar Khan and march on Delhi
localization.event.gujarat_independence.option.muzaff: Proclaim Zafar Khan Sultan Muzaffar Shah
localization.event.gujarat_independence.option.remain: Keep sending the revenue to Delhi
localization.event.hafsid_zayyanid_war.desc: Abu Faris, master of Ifriqiya, takes Algiers and then marches west, setting his own Zayyanid nominees on the throne of Tlemcen in 1424 and again in 1431. For a time the Hafsids are the leading power of the Maghreb.
localization.event.hafsid_zayyanid_war.name: Abu Faris in Tlemcen
localization.event.hafsid_zayyanid_war.option.hold_to: Keep to Ifriqiya and its trade
localization.event.hafsid_zayyanid_war.option.install: Set a Hafsid nominee on Tlemcen's throne
localization.event.hafsids_retake_tripoli.desc: The Hafsid sultan Abu Faris ends the rule of Tripoli's local lords and puts a Hafsid governor in the last great Ifriqiyan port outside Tunis, with its customs and the eastern route.
localization.event.hafsids_retake_tripoli.name: Abu Faris retakes Tripoli
localization.event.hafsids_retake_tripoli.option.acce: Accept the lords' homage and tribute
localization.event.hafsids_retake_tripoli.option.inst: Install a Hafsid governor in Tripoli
localization.event.ho_dynasty.desc: The Trần court never recovered from Champa's sacks, and the minister Hồ Quý Ly gathered power through the 1380s and 1390s, purged the Trần loyalists and moved the capital to Thanh Hóa. On 23 March 1400 he deposed the child emperor and proclaimed the Hồ dynasty, with sweeping reforms of land, coinage and the army.
localization.event.ho_dynasty.name: Hồ Quý Ly takes the throne
localization.event.ho_dynasty.option.ho_regency_refor: Rule as regent and reform in the Trần name
localization.event.ho_dynasty.option.ho_usurpation: Hồ Quý Ly deposes the Trần and founds the Hồ dynasty
localization.event.ho_takes_amaravati.desc: With Chế Bồng Nga dead and Champa divided, Hồ Quý Ly's armies marched south in 1402 and forced the Cham king to give up Amaravati, the land around modern Quảng Nam. The Viets settled it at once, pushing the frontier deep into the old Cham heartland.
localization.event.ho_takes_amaravati.name: Hồ takes Amaravati
localization.event.ho_takes_amaravati.option.cham_tri: Take tribute and leave the frontier
localization.event.hokuzan_falls.desc: Shō Hashi of Chūzan marches on Nakijin and destroys Hokuzan, the northern kingdom of Okinawa, and its king Han'anchi.
localization.event.hokuzan_falls.name: Fall of Hokuzan
localization.event.hu_weiyong_purge.desc: Hongwu accuses his chancellor Hu Weiyong of treason, executes him and thousands of others, and abolishes the Secretariat, so that the ministries answer to the throne alone.
localization.event.hu_weiyong_purge.name: Purge of Hu Weiyong
localization.event.jaunpur_independence.desc: In 1394 the eunuch Malik Sarwar was made Malik-ush-Sharq, lord of the east, to put down the revolts of Awadh and Bihar. With Delhi in civil war he ruled from Jaunpur in his own name, and his heirs took the title of sultan.
localization.event.jaunpur_independence.name: Jaunpur's independence
localization.event.jaunpur_independence.option.bind_h: Bind the lord of the east as a vassal
localization.event.jaunpur_independence.option.hold_t: Hold Awadh and Bihar under the throne
localization.event.jaunpur_independence.option.sarwar: Make Sarwar lord of the east, and lose it
localization.event.jayasthiti_malla_takes_throne.desc: Jayasthiti Malla, long the power behind Jayarjuna, deposed him in 1382 and ruled the whole valley. Tradition credits him with ordering Newar society into castes and fixing the land laws.
localization.event.jayasthiti_malla_takes_throne.name: Jayasthiti Malla takes the throne
localization.event.jayasthiti_malla_takes_throne.opti: Keep ruling through the old king
Take the crown and codify the realm
localization.event.jingnan_war.desc: Jianwen strips his uncles of their fiefs one by one. Zhu Di, Prince of Yan, rises at Beiping in 1399 'to clear the emperor's side', takes Nanjing in 1402, and reigns as the Yongle Emperor while Jianwen vanishes in the burning palace.
localization.event.jingnan_war.name: Jingnan campaign
localization.event.jingnan_war.option.yan_takes_nanji: The Prince of Yan takes Nanjing
localization.event.joseon_founded.desc: Four years after Wihwado, Yi Seong-gye takes the throne from the last Goryeo king. His dynasty, renamed Joseon, breaks the great estates with the Rank Land Law, moves the capital to Hanyang and seeks investiture from Ming.
localization.event.joseon_founded.name: Founding of Joseon
localization.event.jurchen_guards.desc: Yongle wins over the Jurchen chiefs of the Sungari and Tumen with titles and markets: the Jianzhou Guard in 1403, the Haixi guards after it, and the Nurgan regional command on the Amur in 1411, drawing chiefs such as Möngke Temür away from Joseon.
localization.event.jurchen_guards.name: Jurchen guards
localization.event.kano_tributary_to_bornu.desc: Settled west of Lake Chad, Bornu is now Kano's neighbour. In the 1420s to 1430s the Kano Chronicle has Kano paying tribute to the mai, and Bornu's horsemen and Kanuri traders reach the Hausa cities.
localization.event.kano_tributary_to_bornu.name: Kano pays tribute to Bornu
localization.event.kano_tributary_to_bornu.option.pay: Pay tribute and open the road to Bornu
localization.event.kano_tributary_to_bornu.option.ref: Refuse the mai and man the walls
localization.event.kapilendra_usurpation.desc: In 1434-35 Kapilendra, a general of the last Eastern Ganga king Bhanudeva IV, seized the throne of Odisha. As Gajapati he turned the kingdom into a conquering power that soon reached the Godavari and beyond.
localization.event.kapilendra_usurpation.name: Kapilendra founds the Gajapati line
localization.event.kapilendra_usurpation.option.civil: The generals fight for the throne
localization.event.kapilendra_usurpation.option.kapil: Kapilendra takes the throne as Gajapati
localization.event.katehar_revolt.desc: In 1380 Kharku, a Rajput chief of Katehar, murdered the governor of Badaun and his kin. Firuz Shah marched in person, laid the country waste for years and built a fort at Firuzpur to hold the Doab.
localization.event.katehar_revolt.name: The Katehar revolt
localization.event.katehar_revolt.option.pardon_khark: Accept Kharku's submission and spare the land
localization.event.katehar_revolt.option.punish_kateh: Lay Katehar waste and fortify the Doab
localization.event.khami_rises.desc: As Great Zimbabwe fades, the south-west of the plateau goes its own way. The Torwa build a new stone capital at Khami and inherit the western gold and cattle country.
localization.event.khami_rises.name: Torwa rises at Khami
localization.event.khami_rises.option.keep_the_west_i: Keep the Torwa lords as tributaries
localization.event.khami_rises.option.torwa_rule_from: Let the west go to the Torwa at Khami
localization.event.khandesh_breaks_away.desc: After Timur's sack of Delhi, Malik Raja Faruqi's son Nasir Khan ruled Khandesh as his own, founding Burhanpur in 1399. Khandesh lived on between Gujarat, Malwa and the Bahmanis by playing them against each other.
localization.event.khandesh_breaks_away.name: Khandesh breaks away
localization.event.khandesh_breaks_away.option.procla: Rule Khandesh in our own name
localization.event.kongo_founded.desc: Lukeni lua Nimi, a young lord from Vungu or Mpemba Kasi, crosses to the Mbanza Kongo plateau and takes its market town. Allied by marriage with the Nsaku Lau of Mbata, he founds the kingdom of Kongo (c.1390, by tradition).
localization.event.kongo_founded.name: Lukeni lua Nimi founds Kongo
localization.event.kongo_founded.option.take_mbanza_k: Take Mbanza Kongo with the Mbata alliance
localization.event.kongo_founded.option.under_the_tio: Rule under the ritual seniority of the Tio king
localization.event.kongo_provinces_joined.desc: The manikongo brings Mpangu, Nsundi, Mbamba and Soyo under Kongo, naming his own kin as governors, taking nzimbu shells from Luanda island as money and copper from the north (c.1400 to the 1440s, reconstructed).
localization.event.kongo_provinces_joined.name: Kongo gathers its provinces
localization.event.kongo_provinces_joined.option.appo: Name royal kin as governors of the provinces
localization.event.kongo_provinces_joined.option.bind: Bind the provincial lords by marriage
localization.event.kongo_provinces_joined.option.take: Take homage from Kakongo across the river
localization.event.koryaku_coup.desc: Shiba Yoshimasa and the shugo who resent the kanrei Hosokawa Yoriyuki march on Kyoto and force the young shogun Yoshimitsu to dismiss him. Shiba becomes kanrei, and Yoshimitsu begins to rule in his own right.
localization.event.koryaku_coup.name: Kōryaku coup
localization.event.kotte_founded.desc: Parakramabahu VI took the throne c.1412 and ruled from Alagakkonara's fortress at Kotte near the coast, leaving the hill country to a dependent court at Kandy. He went on to conquer Jaffna in 1450 and unite the island.
localization.event.kotte_founded.name: Parakramabahu VI at Kotte
localization.event.kotte_founded.option.seat_at_kotte: Move the court to Kotte and leave the hills to Kandy
localization.event.kotte_founded.option.stay_at_gampo: Keep the court in the hills at Gampola
localization.event.lam_son_uprising.desc: Lê Lợi, a landowner of Thanh Hóa, rises against Ming rule in 1418. After a decade of war he destroys the relief armies at Chi Lăng in 1427; Ming withdraws, and he founds the Lê dynasty as a tributary of the empire.
localization.event.lam_son_uprising.name: Lam Sơn uprising
localization.event.lam_son_uprising.option.hold_jiaoz: Send more armies to hold Jiaozhi
localization.event.majapahit_sacks_singapura.desc: Around 1398 a Javanese fleet fell on Singapura, the port on Temasek that had grown rich on the Strait trade and looked to Siam as much as to Java. The Malay Annals tell of treachery inside the walls; the city was sacked and its last ruler, Parameswara, fled up the coast with his Orang Laut followers.
localization.event.majapahit_sacks_singapura.name: Majapahit sacks Singapura
localization.event.majapahit_sacks_singapura.option.s: Sack Singapura and drive out its ruler
localization.event.majapahit_sacks_singapura.option.t: Demand tribute and leave the port standing
localization.event.malacca_founded.desc: Parameswara, driven from Singapura, settled around 1400 at a fishing village on the Bertam river with his Orang Laut followers. Sheltered by the monsoon winds and soon by Ming envoys, Malacca grew within a generation into the great entrepot of the Strait.
localization.event.malacca_founded.name: Founding of Malacca
localization.event.malacca_founded.option.exile_fades: The exiles scatter and the Strait trade stays with Java
localization.event.malacca_founded.option.found_malac: Found Malacca and seek the Ming emperor's protection
Found Malacca as a tributary of Siam
localization.event.mali_succession_crisis.desc: Mansa Musa II dies in 1387 after years in which his vizier Mari Djata held the real power. Usurpers follow, among them the vizier Sandaki, before Maghan III restores the line around 1390. Mali's hold on its Sahel cities loosens.
localization.event.mali_succession_crisis.name: Mali's succession crisis
localization.event.mali_succession_crisis.option.figh: Let the princes fight it out
localization.event.mali_succession_crisis.option.rall: Rally the court to the Keita heir
localization.event.mali_succession_crisis.option.the_: Let the vizier Sandaki take the throne
localization.event.malwa_independence.desc: Dilawar Khan Ghuri, Delhi's governor of Malwa, sheltered the fugitive Sultan Mahmud at Dhar after Timur's sack, then ruled as an independent king from c.1401. His son Hushang Shah moved the capital to Mandu.
localization.event.malwa_independence.name: Malwa's independence
localization.event.malwa_independence.option.dilawar_: Dilawar Khan rules Malwa as his own
localization.event.malwa_independence.option.shelter_: Shelter the sultan and stay his vassal
localization.event.marinid_attack_on_tlemcen.desc: With Morocco reunited, Fez turns on its old Zayyanid rival. Marinid armies take Tlemcen in 1384, and in 1389 they back Abu Tashufin's revolt against his father Abu Hammu II, who is killed. Tlemcen pays tribute to Fez.
localization.event.marinid_attack_on_tlemcen.name: The Marinids march on Tlemcen
localization.event.marinid_attack_on_tlemcen.option.b: Back Abu Tashufin against his father
localization.event.marinid_attack_on_tlemcen.option.l: Leave Tlemcen to its own quarrels
localization.event.marinid_attack_on_tlemcen.option.t: Besiege Tlemcen and rule it from Fez
localization.event.marrakesh_reunited.desc: Sultan Abu al-Abbas of Fez marches south against his rival Marinid, Abd al-Rahman, who has held Marrakesh and the south since the partition of 1374. Marrakesh falls and the Marinid realm is one again (1382/83 or 1386).
localization.event.marrakesh_reunited.name: Fez takes Marrakesh
localization.event.marrakesh_reunited.option.accept_h: Leave Abd al-Rahman Marrakesh as a vassal
localization.event.marrakesh_reunited.option.keep_the: Make a truce and keep the partition
localization.event.marrakesh_reunited.option.storm_ma: Storm Marrakesh and end the partition
localization.event.masina_settled.desc: Fulbe herders under the Dikko ardos settle the pastures of the inland Niger delta, the land of Masina. Mali, weakened at court, takes tribute from them rather than driving them out.
localization.event.masina_settled.name: The Fulbe settle Masina
localization.event.masina_settled.option.drive_the_he: Drive the herders out of the delta
localization.event.masina_settled.option.grant_pastur: Grant the delta pastures for tribute
localization.event.meitoku_rebellion.desc: The Yamana hold eleven of Japan's sixty-six provinces. Yoshimitsu sets the family against itself, provokes Yamana Ujikiyo into attacking Kyoto and destroys him at Uchino, cutting the house down to three provinces.
localization.event.meitoku_rebellion.name: Meitoku rebellion
localization.event.meitoku_rebellion.option.provoke_a: Provoke the Yamana and crush them
localization.event.mexica_tepanec_marriage.desc: Huitzilihuitl of Tenochtitlan asks Tezozómoc for a daughter. The marriage eases the Mexica tribute and ties the island city to Azcapotzalco's house.
localization.event.mexica_tepanec_marriage.name: A Tepanec queen for Tenochtitlan
localization.event.ming_capital_beijing.desc: Yongle rebuilds his old princely seat as Beijing, with the Forbidden City and a restored Grand Canal, and moves the court there in 1421 to face the Mongols. Nanjing remains a secondary capital.
localization.event.ming_capital_beijing.name: Capital to Beijing
localization.event.ming_conquest_of_dai_viet.desc: Hồ Quý Ly has usurped the Trần, whom Ming had invested. Yongle sends Zhang Fu and Mu Sheng south in 1406; they capture the Hồ in 1407 and annex the country as the province of Jiaozhi.
localization.event.ming_conquest_of_dai_viet.name: Ming in Đại Việt
localization.event.ming_conquest_of_dai_viet.option.a: Annex it as the province of Jiaozhi
localization.event.ming_conquest_of_dai_viet.option.r: Restore a Trần prince as vassal
localization.event.ming_intervention_ceylon_1411.desc: In 1411 Alagakkonara of Gampola tried to seize Zheng He's fleet; Zheng He took the king and his court captive to Nanjing. The Ming named a new king and Ceylon sent tribute for some decades.
localization.event.ming_intervention_ceylon_1411.name: Zheng He in Ceylon
localization.event.ming_intervention_ceylon_1411.opti: Receive the envoys and send tribute
localization.event.ming_takes_yunnan.desc: The last Yuan province inside China falls: Fu Youde, Lan Yu and Mu Ying march from Guizhou, take Kunming in January 1382 and Dali that spring. Basalawarmi, the Yuan Prince of Liang, kills himself and the Mu family begins its long rule of the province.
localization.event.ming_takes_yunnan.name: Ming takes Yunnan
localization.event.ming_takes_yunnan.option.accept_th: Accept the prince's submission for a Ming title
localization.event.mutapa_formed.desc: Short of salt and land, and drawn by the Zambezi trade, Nyatsimba Mutota leads a Zimbabwe-culture elite north to the Dande and conquers the northern plateau. His title, Mwene Mutapa, names the new kingdom (c.1430, by tradition).
localization.event.mutapa_formed.name: Mutota goes north: Mutapa
localization.event.mutapa_formed.option.a_cadet_kingd: Send a cadet house north to rule in tribute
localization.event.mutapa_formed.option.mutota_moves_: Let Mutota lead his people north
localization.event.mutapa_formed.option.stay_on_the_p: Hold everyone at the old capital
localization.event.naghachu_surrenders.desc: With Yunnan taken, Feng Sheng leads a great army beyond the Liao. Naghachu, the Yuan commander who had held Manchuria for the khan since 1368, surrenders in 1387 and takes a Ming title, leaving the khan without his eastern army.
localization.event.naghachu_surrenders.name: Naghachu surrenders
localization.event.naghachu_surrenders.option.join_th: Take the army north to the khan
localization.event.oei_invasion.desc: When wokou from Tsushima raid again, the retired king Taejong sends 17,000 men to the island. The Sō submit, and the trade licences of the 1443 Gyehae treaty follow.
localization.event.oei_invasion.name: Ōei invasion of Tsushima
localization.event.oei_invasion.option.license_the_so: License the Sō to trade instead
localization.event.oei_rebellion.desc: Ōuchi Yoshihiro, lord of six provinces and of the trade with Korea, refuses the shogun's summons and fortifies Sakai, counting on the Kamakura kubo. Yoshimitsu storms the town and Yoshihiro dies in the fighting.
localization.event.oei_rebellion.name: Ōei rebellion
localization.event.oei_rebellion.option.ouchi_holds_t: The Ōuchi hold the western straits
localization.event.paregreg_war.desc: From 1404 to 1406 Wikramawardhana's western court and Bhre Wirabhumi's eastern court fought for Majapahit. The west won and Bhre Wirabhumi was beheaded, but the war cost Java its grip on the archipelago just as the Ming fleets arrived; Zheng He's men were caught in the fighting in the east.
localization.event.paregreg_war.name: The Paregreg war
localization.event.paregreg_war.option.courts_reconci: Buy peace between the two courts
localization.event.rathores_take_mandore.desc: Rao Chunda of the Rathores won Mandore c.1395, by tradition as the dowry of a Parihar bride, while Delhi's garrisons in Rajputana were left to themselves. His sister Hansa Bai later married Rana Lakha of Mewar.
localization.event.rathores_take_mandore.name: The Rathores take Mandore
localization.event.rathores_take_mandore.option.chund: Chunda takes Mandore and allies with Mewar
localization.event.rathores_take_mandore.option.ratho: The Rathores hold Mandore under Mewar
localization.event.razadarit_reunites_hanthawaddy.des: Razadarit took Pegu's throne in 1384 when the Mon lands were split: Byattaba held Martaban and Laukpya the western delta. By about 1390 he had taken both, though Laukpya's call to Ava for help began the long war with the north.
localization.event.razadarit_reunites_hanthawaddy.opt: Leave the rebel lords in place as tributaries
Laukpya calls Ava to the delta
localization.event.reddi_kingdom_splits.desc: After Anavema Reddi's death the Kondavidu court quarrelled over the succession, and c.1395 Kataya Vema made the Godavari country around Rajahmundry a separate Reddi kingdom.
localization.event.reddi_kingdom_splits.name: The Reddi kingdom splits
localization.event.reddi_kingdom_splits.option.appana: Grant Rajahmundry as a dependent appanage
localization.event.reddi_kingdom_splits.option.keep_t: Keep the realm whole by force
localization.event.ryukyu_united.desc: Shō Hashi defeats Taromai of Nanzan and unites Okinawa as the Kingdom of Ryukyu, with its seat at Shuri. With Ming tribute ships and the port of Naha, the kingdom becomes the entrepôt between China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia.
localization.event.ryukyu_united.name: Ryukyu united
localization.event.sack_of_delhi.desc: Timur crossed the Indus in 1398, saying the sultans were too lenient with their Hindu subjects. He routed Mahmud Shah Tughlaq and Mallu Iqbal outside Delhi in December, sacked the city for days and left Khizr Khan to govern Multan and the Punjab.
localization.event.sack_of_delhi.name: Timur sacks Delhi
localization.event.sack_of_delhi.option.demand_tribut: Take tribute and turn back west
localization.event.sack_of_delhi.option.sack_and_with: Sack Delhi and leave Khizr Khan in the Punjab
localization.event.sack_of_delhi.option.take_the_punj: Annex the Punjab to the empire
localization.event.sayfawa_flight_to_bornu.desc: The Bulala kill one Sayfawa mai after another. Mai Umar b. Idris gives up Njimi and leads the court west of Lake Chad into Bornu, where the dynasty survives through decades of feuds between its branches.
localization.event.sayfawa_flight_to_bornu.name: The Sayfawa leave Kanem
localization.event.sayfawa_flight_to_bornu.option.pay: Pay tribute to the Bulala to keep Kanem
localization.event.sayfawa_flight_to_bornu.option.wit: Abandon Njimi and rebuild west of Lake Chad
localization.event.sayyid_delhi.desc: When the last Tughlaq sultan died in 1412 the nobles chose Daulat Khan Lodi. In 1414 Khizr Khan, Timur's governor of Multan, took Delhi and ruled as the deputy of Shah Rukh, founding the Sayyid dynasty.
localization.event.sayyid_delhi.name: The Sayyids take Delhi
localization.event.sayyid_delhi.option.claim_the_thro: Rule Delhi in our own name
localization.event.sayyid_delhi.option.rule_as_timuri: Take Delhi as Shah Rukh's deputy
localization.event.sayyid_delhi.option.stay_in_multan: Hold Multan and leave Delhi to the Lodis
localization.event.songhai_breaks_from_mali.desc: The Sunni kings of Kukiya, long tributary to Mali, take Gao and stop paying. The river kingdom of Songhai is free again and begins to raid west into Mali's lands. The date is uncertain, between the 1390s and c.1400.
localization.event.songhai_breaks_from_mali.name: Songhai breaks from Mali
localization.event.songhai_breaks_from_mali.option.pa: Keep paying and raid Mali's villages
localization.event.songhai_breaks_from_mali.option.ri: Rise against Mali in open war
localization.event.songhai_breaks_from_mali.option.ta: Take Gao and stop the tribute
localization.event.southern_line_passed_over.desc: Against the promise of 1392, the retired emperor Go-Komatsu has his own son Shōkō crowned. Go-Kameyama flees to Yoshino and Southern loyalists rise in Ise and the mountains for decades.
localization.event.southern_line_passed_over.name: Southern line passed over
localization.event.southern_line_passed_over.option.c: Crown Shōkō of the Northern line
localization.event.sukhothai_absorbed.desc: When Maha Thammaracha IV died in 1438, Ayutthaya did not name another king of Sukhothai. Borommarachathirat II sent his son Ramesuan, born of a Sukhothai princess, to govern at Phitsanulok, and the old kingdom became a province of Ayutthaya; Lan Na courted its restless lords.
localization.event.sukhothai_absorbed.name: Sukhothai absorbed
localization.event.sukhothai_absorbed.option.keep_suk: Crown a new vassal king of Sukhothai
localization.event.sukhothai_absorbed.option.make_vic: Send Prince Ramesuan to govern at Phitsanulok
localization.event.sukhothai_absorbed.option.sukhotha: Sukhothai's lords call on Lan Na
localization.event.suphannaphum_takes_ayutthaya.desc: Ayutthaya's throne passed between two rival houses, the U Thong line of Lavo and the Suphannaphum line. In 1409 Intharacha, a Suphannaphum prince known at the Ming court, deposed Ramrachathirat with a minister's help; his line ruled from then on and pressed hard on Sukhothai and Angkor.
localization.event.suphannaphum_takes_ayutthaya.name: Suphannaphum takes Ayutthaya
localization.event.suphannaphum_takes_ayutthaya.optio: The two houses fight for the throne
Intharacha seizes the throne for Suphannaphum
The U Thong line holds the throne
localization.event.tariacuri_unites_patzcuaro.desc: Tariácuri of the Uacúsecha gathers the Pátzcuaro basin for the god Curicaueri, breaking Curínguaro and the island lords. At his death the realm passes to his son and two nephews.
localization.event.tariacuri_unites_patzcuaro.name: Tariácuri unites the Pátzcuaro basin
Unite the basin under a single heir
Unite the basin and share it among three heirs
localization.event.tepanec_conquest_of_texcoco.desc: Tezozómoc turns on the Acolhua, the only rival for leadership of the Basin. Ixtlilxochitl of Texcoco is killed and his son Nezahualcoyotl flees into exile.
localization.event.tepanec_conquest_of_texcoco.name: The Tepanec war on Texcoco
localization.event.tepanec_conquest_of_texcoco.option: Conquer Texcoco and kill its king
Offer Ixtlilxochitl a daughter and junior rank
localization.event.tepanec_expansion.desc: Tezozómoc of Azcapotzalco sends his armies, with Mexica warriors fighting for a share of the spoils, against the southern lake towns, Cuauhnahuac and Chalco.
localization.event.tepanec_expansion.name: Tepanec expansion
localization.event.tepanec_expansion.option.conquer_w: Conquer the lake towns with Mexica warriors
localization.event.tepanec_expansion.option.rule_by_m: Bind the lake lords by marriage instead
localization.event.tepanec_war.desc: Itzcoatl of Tenochtitlan, Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco and the lords of Tlacopan rise against Maxtla, with help from Huexotzinco. Azcapotzalco falls, and the three cities share the Basin as one alliance.
localization.event.tepanec_war.name: The Tepanec war and the Triple Alliance
localization.event.tepanec_war.option.break_free_alon: Break free alone and fight on
localization.event.tepanec_war.option.form_the_triple: Rise with Texcoco and Tlacopan and destroy Azcapotzalco
localization.event.tomars_take_gwalior.desc: In the disorder after Firuz Shah's death, Bir Singh Deo of the Tomars took the fort of Gwalior, c.1394. The Tomar rajas held it for more than a century, paying tribute only when Delhi was strong.
localization.event.tomars_take_gwalior.name: The Tomars take Gwalior
localization.event.tomars_take_gwalior.option.tomars_: The Tomars hold Gwalior for themselves
Leave the fort to the Tomars for tribute
localization.event.treasure_fleet_on_the_swahili_coas: Zheng He's fleets call at Mogadishu, Barawa and Malindi. Malindi's envoys take a giraffe to the Yongle emperor, and the coast's sultans trade ivory and ambergris for silk and porcelain.
Ming fleets on the Swahili coast
Send envoys and a giraffe to the emperor
Trade with the fleet but send no tribute
localization.event.treasure_voyages.desc: To show the world his Mandate, Yongle sends Zheng He with hundreds of ships and some 27,000 men across the Indian Ocean. Seven voyages from 1405 to 1433 reach Malacca, Calicut, Hormuz, Aden and the Swahili coast, bringing envoys and tribute to the court.
localization.event.treasure_voyages.name: Treasure voyages
localization.event.treasure_voyages.option.open_priva: Lift the sea ban for private traders
localization.event.tuareg_take_timbuktu.desc: Mali can no longer defend the Niger bend. The Maghsharen Tuareg under Akil take Timbuktu and later Walata, and leave the city's Timbuktu-koi to govern it for a share of the revenue.
localization.event.tuareg_take_timbuktu.name: Akil takes Timbuktu
localization.event.tuareg_take_timbuktu.option.abando: Give up Timbuktu to the Tuareg
localization.event.tuareg_take_timbuktu.option.buy_of: Pay Akil's raiders to stay in the desert
localization.event.tuareg_take_timbuktu.option.send_t: Send the army north to hold the city
localization.event.tughlaq_succession_war.desc: Between 1388 and 1394 four sultans held Delhi in turn, and from 1394 two rival sultans ruled from Delhi and Firozabad. The governors stopped sending revenue and Sindh stopped paying tribute.
localization.event.tughlaq_succession_war.name: The Tughlaq succession wars
localization.event.tughlaq_succession_war.option.stro: Back a strongman to hold the capital
localization.event.tughlaq_succession_war.option.two_: Let the factions fight it out
localization.event.vijayanagara_annexes_kondavidu.des: Weakened by its quarrels with Rajahmundry, the Velamas and Odisha, the Reddi kingdom of Kondavidu fell to Deva Raya II's armies c.1424, giving Vijayanagara the Krishna delta.
localization.event.vijayanagara_annexes_kondavidu.opt: Take tribute and leave the Reddis on the throne
localization.event.vijayanagara_bahmani_wars.desc: The Bahmanis and Vijayanagara fought over the rich land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra, with its forts of Raichur and Mudgal, in 1398, 1406, 1417-20 and 1443. Each war ended in tribute or a truce, never a lasting conquest.
localization.event.vijayanagara_bahmani_wars.name: War for the Raichur doab
localization.event.vijayanagara_takes_goa.desc: While the Bahmani court was still shaken by the murders of two sultans in 1378, Harihara II's minister Madhava seized Goa and the Konkan ports, through which the Arab warhorses came.
localization.event.vijayanagara_takes_goa.name: Vijayanagara takes Goa
localization.event.vijayanagara_takes_goa.option.seiz: Seize Goa and the horse trade
localization.event.vijayanagara_takes_goa.option.sett: Settle the conquered Tamil country first
localization.event.wendat_alliance.desc: The Attignawantan and the Attigneenongnahac, the two largest Wendat peoples, join in an alliance for defence against raids from the south.
localization.event.wendat_alliance.name: The Wendat alliance
localization.event.wendat_alliance.option.join_the_tw: Join the two peoples in one alliance
localization.event.wendat_alliance.option.move_the_vi: Move the villages north and stay apart
localization.event.wihwado_retreat.desc: When Ming claims the land north of Cheolryeong, Choe Yeong sends the Goryeo army against Liaodong. Yi Seong-gye halts on Wihwa island in the Yalu, turns back, takes the capital and deposes King U.
localization.event.wihwado_retreat.name: Retreat from Wihwado
localization.event.wihwado_retreat.option.turn_back_a: Turn the army back at Wihwado
localization.event.wihwado_retreat.option.yield_to_th: Yield the north without a fight
localization.event.yellow_registers.desc: Hongwu orders a census of every household in the empire, grouped into tithings of 110 households that serve in turn; the Yellow Registers of 1381 and the fish-scale land maps of 1387 become the tax base of the dynasty.
localization.event.yellow_registers.name: The Yellow Registers
localization.event.yellow_registers.option.keep_the_y: Make do with the Yuan rolls
localization.event.yoshimitsu_king_of_japan.desc: Yoshimitsu sends envoys to Ming and is invested as King of Japan in 1402. The tally trade that follows brings copper coin, silk and books, at the price of a vassal's title the court nobles resent.
localization.event.yoshimitsu_king_of_japan.name: Yoshimitsu, King of Japan
localization.event.yoshimitsu_king_of_japan.option.ac: Accept investiture and the tally trade
